hints.title: Name the three claims
hints.body: Use H for the displayed parameter inequality, S for the stationary points lying on opposite sides of the axis, and R for three distinct real roots.
hints.recap: A proof of “R if H” must start from H and justify reaching R.
hints.pitfall: “R if H” and “H if R” ask for opposite directions.
hints.pause: Translate the target and each numbered implication into arrows between H, S and R.

recall.reminder: Track what is known and what is needed at each proof stage.

hints.title: Check whether the arrows connect
hints.body: After verifying the derivative and stationary-point coordinates, compare the implications actually stated in II and III with the conclusion asserted in IV.
hints.recap: Knowing that two claims each imply a third does not automatically connect the first two claims.
hints.pitfall: An implication may be mathematically true yet still be the wrong direction for the proof being attempted.
hints.pause: Determine whether the stated arrows form the required chain, and identify exactly which additional direction would be needed if they do not.

recall.reminder: A proof needs a chain whose output at one stage supplies the input of the next.

solution:
The derivative is x(3x+2a), so the stationary inputs are 0 and −2a/3, with heights b and b+4a3/27. Since a≠0, these are distinct turning points.

Write H for the parameter inequality, S for opposite-sign stationary heights, and R for three distinct roots. Step II proves H⇒S, while step III states R⇒S. These arrows do not establish H⇒R.

The missing link is S⇒R, the converse of step III. For a cubic, opposite-sign turning heights do force three crossings, but that direction has to be established or stated. Answer: E.
knowledgePattern: Distinguish a necessary turning-height condition from the sufficient direction needed
